title.value: ROBOETHICS FOR EVERYONE - A HANDS - ON TEACHING MODULE FOR K-12 AND BEYOND
title.justification: The title reflects the focus of the paper on creating and delivering an educational module intended to teach roboethics to a wide audience, including K-12 students.
title.quote: ROBOETHICS FOR EVERYONE ^{–} A HANDS - ON TEACHING MODULE FOR K-12 AND BEYOND

analysis.description: This paper presents a teaching module designed to introduce K-12 students and general audiences to the concepts of roboethics. It emphasizes the ethical implications of AI and robotics, aiming to foster understanding without requiring advanced technical knowledge. The module was delivered in a workshop format and successfully promoted critical thinking and ethical considerations among students.

type.justification: The paper includes the development and implementation of a teaching module and its workshop, providing observational insights on student engagement and learning outcomes.
type.quote: We conducted a workshop using the paper-based delivery modality, which is described in Section 4.

name.justification: The paper focuses on the ethics of artificial intelligence and robotic systems, establishing it as the core research field.
name.quote: In this section, we briefly provide an overview of AI ethics and roboethics.

name.justification: The study delves into how humans interact with robots and the ethical implications, thus being a significant sub-field.
name.quote: Keywords: human-robot interaction, roboethics, teaching module, workshop.

name.justification: Processing is explicitly mentioned as a tool used to develop the software simulation platform in the teaching module.
name.quote: The software simulation was developed using Processing [33] and Java; The project's code can be found on GitHub [34].

referenced_paper_title.justification: Processing is correctly referenced to its official site which provides tools and references for its use.
